column2: {n} made chicken noises at you all week.
{n} just got braces and is embarrassed to smile.
{n} smiled for the first time all week.
{n} didn't talk to you for days.
{n} wants you to do a duet with {him} at the talent show.
Your voice cracked. {n} kept singing to cover for you.
You did the robot. People still talk about it.
{n} wants you both to fake sick and skip the field trip.
You spent the day playing games at home.
The school nurse saw right through you.
You both got lost in the gift shop.
{n} wants you to come to a party at an older kid's house.
The cops showed up. You hid in a closet for an hour.
You left right before things got crazy.
{n} just got {his} license and wants to take you for a drive.
{n} hit a mailbox. You're both fine. The mailbox is not.
You got passed by a bicycle.
{n} just got dumped and showed up at your door crying.
{n} said you're the only one who gets {him}.
{n} got a fake ID and wants to get you one too.
It worked. You felt like a criminal mastermind.
{n} rolled {his} eyes but thought about it.
{n} wants to copy your homework. Again.
{n} copied someone else's and got caught.
{n} wants to go to prom as a group of friends.
You danced all night. Best prom ever.
You stayed home and watched the photos roll in.
{n} wants to take a road trip after graduation.
Three states, two flat tires, one perfect summer.
The car broke down halfway. Expensive tow.
Turn it into a camping trip
You saw a bear. From very far away.
Someone started a rumor that you and {n} secretly hate each other.
It was the class gossip. Justice was served.
You accused the wrong person. Awkward.
{n} wants to apply to the same college as you.
Make a pact to go together
You pinky swore. It's legally binding.
Say you need your own path
{n} said {his} essay is way better now.
{n} is moving and needs help carrying a couch up four flights of stairs.
{n} asked you to be in {his} wedding party.
Your speech made everyone cry. In a good way.
Your speech made everyone cry. In a bad way.
You tore up the dance floor instead.
{n} wants you to invest in {his} startup: an app where dogs rate their walks.
A big company bought the app! You made money!
The app flopped. Your money is gone.
{n} asked to borrow money until payday.
{n} hugged you for a really long time.
{n} invited you to a board game night.
You won Monopoly. Friendships were tested.
You flipped the board. Not your proudest moment.
Everyone wants you back next week.
{n} never did the dishes. Not once.
It was fine. You stayed friends.
{n} scored two tickets to a sold-out concert.
You lost your voice from screaming.
Go and pay {him} back for the ticket
{n} hasn't texted back in three weeks.
{n} was going through a hard time and was grateful you reached out.
Show up at {his} door with tacos
{n} wants you to be {his} gym buddy.
You were sore for a week.
Brunch is cardio if you walk there.
{n} just bought a red sports car and wants to take you for a ride.
It was way too fast. Your back hurts.
{n} invited you to {his} kid's piano recital.
{n}'s kid waved at you from the stage.
{n} wants to go to your high school reunion together.
Everyone looked older. You looked great.
Your old bully is a millionaire now. Great.
{n} gave you all the gossip afterward.
Go and live at the snack table
{n} is going through a divorce and needs a place to stay.
{n} stayed three months. You became even closer.
Say it's not a good time
{n} wants you to take golf lessons together.
You hit one good shot. That's all you need.
Drifting a golf cart is a sport now.
{n} had a health scare and asked you to come to {his} appointment.
It was nothing serious. {n} cried with relief.
It's serious. {n} is so grateful you were there.
{n} wants to open a restaurant with you.
The restaurant closed after a year. You lost your investment.
{n} made a bucket list. Item one: skydiving, with you.
You screamed the whole way down. Incredible.
Rough landing. You sprained your ankle.
{n}'s kids just moved out and {he} is lonely.
{n} wants to hit the 4pm early bird special at the diner.
Two meals for one price. Life is good.
Say 4pm is too late for dinner
{n} signed you both up for the senior pickleball league.
You're the pickleball champions of the community center.
You pulled a hamstring. You're benched.
You were a very fair referee.
{n} is convinced the bingo caller is rigging the games.
You were right! Shirley was cheating!
You got banned from bingo for two weeks.
{n} wants to show you 400 photos of {his} grandkids.
It turned into a grandkid photo battle.
{n} wants to go on a senior cruise together.
Half the ship got food poisoning.
You saw the world's largest ball of yarn.
{n} keeps saying "WHAT?" and refuses to get hearing aids.
{n} got them. {He} can hear birds again.
Your throat hurts, but {n} is happy.
{n} asked you to come with {him} to an old friend's funeral.
Everyone laughed at your story. It was a good send-off.
Say there have been too many funerals lately
{n} is moving to Florida and wants you to come too.
{n} sent you a picture of a flamingo.
{n} wants you to teach {him} how to video call {his} grandkids.
It worked! {n} saw {his} grandkids and cried.
{n} only saw {his} own forehead the whole call.
The grandkid set it up in ten seconds.
{n} built a snow fort and declared war on you.
You hit {n} square in the ear!
Together you defeated the whole schoolyard.
{n} found a kitten crying in the woodpile and wants to keep it secret.
Help hide it in the barn
You named it Biscuit. It is the best cat.
Bring it milk from the kitchen
{n} had to give the kitten away.
{n} found a penny in the road and wants to go to the general store.
Add a penny of your own
You bought a whole bag of peppermint sticks.
Say it belongs to someone else
{n} made a kite from newspaper and string and wants to fly it on the hill.
The kite climbed higher than the church steeple!
The kite got stuck in a tree.
{n} let you fly it all afternoon.
It flew. {n} has not let you forget it.
{n} dares you to go inside the old abandoned house on the hill after dark.
You found nothing but bats and cobwebs.
Something moaned upstairs. You both ran all the way home.
{n} came out white as a sheet.
{n} told the whole school you were scared.
{n} wants to put a frog in the schoolmaster's desk.
The schoolmaster leapt clean out of his chair!
You were both caught and kept after school.
The whole class laughed for a week.
{n} got the cane. {He} knows it was you.
{n}'s family calf got loose and {he} needs help catching it before dark.
You caught it by the rope at the edge of the woods.
The calf dragged you through the mud.
Lure it with a bucket of oats
The calf followed you home like a puppy.
{n} wants to sit on the fence and whittle with {his} new pocketknife.
It looked more like a dog, but {n} admired it.
Your names are on that fence post for good.
{n} wants your help writing a love letter to {his} sweetheart.
The sweetheart said yes to a walk after church!
The sweetheart laughed at the poem.
{n} wanted to crawl under the floorboards.
{n} wants to lie about {his} age and join the army.
{n} stayed home. Your talk may have saved {his} life.
{n} was taken on as a blacksmith's apprentice and wants to show you the forge.
{n} made you a horseshoe for luck.
You burned your hand on the iron.
{n} said honest work is nothing to sneer at.
{n} got hold of a dime novel about outlaws and wants to read it with you in the loft.
You read it twice before sunrise.
You knocked over a milk pail in the excitement.
Say it will rot your brain
{n} heard there is gold in the hills and wants you to buy a pick and pan with {him}.
You found a few flakes and a lot of mud.
You found a nugget the size of a pea!
{n} promised to bring you back a nugget.
{n} was insulted by a gentleman and wants you to act as {his} second in a duel.
Nobody fired a shot. {n} is still alive.
Both men fired into the air. Honor was satisfied.
{n} took a ball in the shoulder. {He} will live.
{n} asked you to be godparent to {his} newborn baby.
The baby cried all through the christening. Perfect.
{n} said it would be treasured for generations.
{n} picked a fight with a burly drover at the tavern.
You both walked out with black eyes and your pride.
You were thrown into the street face first.
{n}'s house caught fire in the night.
They stayed with you for a month.
{n} saw you there. {He} will not forget.
{n} says the new railroad line will make you both rich if you buy shares now.
{n} clapped you on the back. Full steam ahead.
The numbers looked shakier than {n} admitted.
{n} cannot read and asked you to read a letter from {his} son at war.
The boy is alive and well. {n} wept with relief.
{n} told you every word to say.
{n} wants you to ride into town with {him} on election day.
The torchlight parade was loud and the speeches were louder.
Neither of you changed your mind.
{n} said you will have no right to complain.
{n}'s old mantel clock has stopped and {he} insists you know how to fix it.
It ticked again! {n} called you a genius.
You now have a pile of springs and an apology to make.
{n} wants a game of chess by the stove at the general store.
You won in twenty moves. {n} demanded a rematch.
{n} has not been this cheerful in years.
{n} moved some of your pieces while you napped.
{n} wants you to witness {his} last will and testament.
{n} said there was nobody {he} trusted more.
{n} said you will just have to wait and see.
Say you don't want to talk of dying
{n} lost {his} spectacles and is sure you took them.
They were on top of {his} head the whole time.
{n} said everything looks blurry and bigger.
{n} found them on {his} head and never apologized.
{n} wants to race wooden hoops down the lane with sticks.
Your hoop rolled all the way to the church door!
Your hoop wobbled into a ditch. {n} won.
{n} challenged you to a game of marbles in the schoolyard.
You played until the school bell rang.
{n} forgot {his} lunch pail and is staring at your bread and cheese.
{n} made a rag doll out of scraps and wants you to name it.
{n} said it was the finest coat in town.
Say it looks like a potato sack
{n} wants to catch frogs down at the creek.
You caught a bullfrog the size of a loaf of bread.
You slipped and fell in the creek. {n} laughed all the way home.
{n} caught three frogs and named them all.
{n} got a switching. {He} won't forget it.
{n} wants to start a secret club with a password that meets in the hayloft.
The password is "turnip." Tell no one.
The great hayloft war has begun.
{n} wants to sneak into old farmer Brown's orchard and steal apples.
You filled your pockets with apples!
The farmer's dog chased you both over the fence.
{n} came back with an armful of apples.
{n} wants to study with you for the schoolhouse spelling bee.
{n} wants to jump off the rocks into the old swimming hole.
The water was freezing. It was glorious.
You scraped your leg on the rocks.
{n} wants you to go with {him} to the barn dance on Saturday.
You danced until the fiddler's strings snapped.
Go but stand by the wall
{n} dragged you onto the floor anyway.
{n} wants you to come on a moonlit hayride with the other young folks.
You sang songs under the stars all the way to the river.
Go and sit with your sweetheart
Your mother was pleased, at least.
{n} was jilted by {his} sweetheart and showed up at your door weeping.
{n} said you're the only true friend {he} has.
Write a nasty letter to the sweetheart
The letter was the talk of the town.
Say there are other fish in the sea
{n} found a jug of moonshine behind the barn and wants you to try it.
It burned all the way down. You coughed for a minute.
You were sick behind the barn all night.
{n} got the strap. {He} knows it was you.
{n} wants to copy your lessons for the schoolmaster. Again.
{n} wants to run off and seek {his} fortune out West.
{n} is raising a new barn and needs every pair of hands.
The barn went up by sundown. There was pie.
Everyone said it was the best stew they'd had.
{n} asked you to stand up for {him} at {his} wedding.
You gave a toast that made the whole church laugh.
Say yes but skip the dancing
{n} asked to borrow money until the harvest comes in.
{n} promised to pay you back after harvest.
{n} invited you to a game of whist by the fire.
You won three hands in a row!
You lost, but it was a fine evening.
The pie was gone in minutes.
{n} has two tickets to the traveling show when it comes through town.
You saw a sword swallower and a bearded lady!
{n} said you didn't have to, but thanked you.
{n} wants you to come hunting deer with {him} in the hills.
You brought home a fine buck.
You came home empty-handed but had a fine time.
Go but just carry the pack
{n}'s child has a terrible fever and {he} begged you to fetch the doctor.
The doctor came in time. The child pulled through.
Sit up with the family all night
{n} wants you to bring a pie to the church social.
Buy a pie at the bakery
{n} wants you to go halves with {him} on a new dry goods store.
{n} shook your hand and promised you a share of the profits.
{n}'s family ran out of firewood in a hard winter.
Bring them a wagonload of wood
{n}'s children were warm again that night.
Invite them to stay with you
The house was crowded but warm.
{n} remembered who helped and who didn't.
{n} wants to sit on the porch and watch the world go by.
You both laughed about the old days.
You both shed a few tears at the graveside.
{n} keeps shouting "WHAT?" and refuses to use an ear trumpet.
The whole street heard your conversation.
{n} thinks you agreed to something. You're not sure what.
{n} wants to tell you every story about {his} grandchildren.
There were a great many grandchildren.
You both agreed your grandchildren are the finest.
{n} swears by a new patent tonic for {his} aching joints.
It made you dizzy for an hour.
{n} sulked, but you may be right.
{n} has won bingo nine weeks in a row. You suspect foul play.
You found extra cards in {his} cardigan!
You won a coupon for pudding.
There's only one chocolate pudding left and {n} is reaching for it.
You both grabbed it. It hit the floor.
{n} saved you {his} pudding the next day.
{n} has a plan to escape the nursing home and wants you in.
You made it out and caught a bus home!
You got as far as the parking lot.
{n} made it to the gas station and back with snacks.
There's a chair yoga class this morning.
You touched your toes. Well, your shins.
The instructor did not appreciate it.
Your new roommate, {n}, snores like a chainsaw.
You got a room with a window!
The nursing home is having a talent show.
You forgot the words but kept humming.
Tough crowd. Half of them were asleep.
{n} did a magic trick with {his} dentures.
{n} keeps saving you a seat at dinner and winking.
You and {n} are the talk of the nursing home.
It was just something in {his} eye.
It's visiting day, but nobody has come to see you.
Your kid came an hour later with cookies.
{n}'s family didn't come either. You kept each other company.
You shared it with the whole hallway.
{n} has hogged the TV remote for three days.
You watched your show in peace.
{n} woke up and chased you with {his} walker.
You now have a TV schedule.
You're hooked on {his} soap opera now.
The nursing home is taking a field trip to the mall.
You walked three laps and bought fudge.
The staff threw you a birthday party.
You talked for 40 minutes. Everyone was patient.
They had to check your file.
{n} challenged you to a wheelchair race down the hallway.
You crashed into the medicine cart.
You waved a napkin as the flag.
The ladies in the lounge are gossiping about {n}.
{n} heard about it and thanked you.
The knitting club wants you to join.
You knitted a very lumpy scarf.
They knitted you a scarf anyway.
Your physical therapist wants you to try walking without your cane.
You made it all the way down the hall!
You wobbled and had to sit down.
They were in {his} cup! {He} thought they were {his}.
{n} wants to play poker for real money.
A local band is playing songs from your youth.
You've still got the moves. Your hip does not.
They played it. You cried a little.
Your grandkids came to visit and look bored.
They were on their phones the whole time.
There was a fire drill at 3am.
You started a sing-along in the parking lot.
You can plant something in the community garden.
Nobody noticed. Everyone was very relaxed.
The night nurse, {n}, is really kind to you.
Your kid yelled at the manager. Fixed.
{n} keeps calling you by the wrong name.
It's movie night, and it's a movie you've seen 50 times.
Some people loved it. Some did not.
{n} claims {he} was once a chess champion.
{n} showed you a trophy from decades ago.
His name was Biscuit. You love him.
Biscuit's handler found him under your bed.
There's a church service in the common room.
The pastor gave you a thumbs up.
Your kids keep asking about your will during visits.
Say it's all going to the cat
{n} says {he} used to be a famous actor.
It's true! {He} was in three movies!
You came in fourth. Out of four.
It's a card from your grandkid!
The nurse handed you the wrong pills.
